And as soon as these great miracles of such a kind appeared, O Great King, the Tathāgatas residing in many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddha-fields, as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges, will turn their attention toward that Dharma-preacher.
And they will offer words of praise, saying: "Excellent, excellent, O noble man!

Excellent indeed, O noble man, you who desire to extensively proclaim this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, which is of such a nature, so profound, so profound in meaning, so profound in its radiance, and endowed with such inconceivable qualities and dharmas."
And these beings will not be endowed with any other roots of merit than those who,
at the very least, shall hear this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras—
let alone those who shall take it up, uphold it, write it down, cause it to be written, recite it, or master it.
They will extensively proclaim, teach, recite, study, and properly attend to it with their minds within the assembly.
Why is that?

Because upon merely hearing this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattvas will become irreversible from unsurpassed [perfect enlightenment].
of perfect enlightenment.

Then, indeed, at that time and on that occasion, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas, residing in their respective Buddha-fields throughout the hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddha-fields in the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā,
spoke these words with one foot, one voice, and one sound to that monk, the Dharma-preacher, as he sat upon his Dharma-seat:
"O noble son, you will approach the seat of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) in a future time. O noble son,

having reached the most excellent and supreme seat of enlightenment and sitting at the foot of the king of trees, you will manifest for all beings throughout the three times— beings who are preeminent in the entire triple world— the various empowerments and foundations resulting from the power of their vows and the practice of austerities."
"O virtuous man, you shall adorn the seat of enlightenment for hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons difficult to practice.
O virtuous man, you shall protect all the triple-thousand great thousandfold world systems.
O virtuous man, seated at the foot of the king of trees, you shall defeat the inconceivable army of Māra, which possesses various deformed shapes, an appearance most loathsome and artificial."

"O virtuous man, having reached the most excellent and supreme seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*), you will fully awaken to the unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment—unsurpassed, tranquil, stainless, and profound.

Seated upon the noble, solid, and adamantine throne (*vajrāsana*), O virtuous man, you will set in motion the twelvefold, unsurpassed wheel of Dharma, which is supremely profound and praised by all people. O virtuous man, you will strike the drum of the unsurpassed treasury of Dharma."
O virtuous man, you shall fill the unsurpassed great conch of the Dharma;
O virtuous man, you shall raise the great banner of the Dharma;
O virtuous man, you shall kindle the unsurpassed torch of the Dharma.
O virtuous one, you shall rain down the unsurpassed great rain of Dharma upon the worthy ones; O virtuous one, you shall conquer many hundreds of thousands of afflictions;
O virtuous one, you shall ferry across many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings from the most terrifying ocean of great fears.
O virtuous man, you will liberate many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings from the wheel of saṃsāra;
O virtuous man, you will please many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Tathāgatas.
When this had been said, the four Great Kings addressed the Blessed One in this way:
"Venerable Blessed One, such are these transgressions against the Dharma of this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras."

"Beholding the qualities that conquer Māra, and seeing that the human king who has planted roots of merit under thousands of Buddhas will, out of compassion, acquire an immeasurable mass of merit, we— the four Great Kings, O Venerable Blessed One— along with our forces and retinues and many hundreds of thousands of yakṣas,
while remaining in our own abodes, were moved by various incense, smoke, creepers, and parasols; and thus, with our bodies invisible, we [proceeded] toward..."

We shall approach the royal palace of that king of men— which has been thoroughly purified by heaps of refined materials, well-sprinkled with various scented waters, and adorned with various ornaments— in order to hear the Dharma;
as will Brahmā Sahāmpati, Śakra the lord of the gods, the great goddess Sarasvatī, and the great goddess Śrī.
And the Earth Goddess Dṛḍhā, the great yakṣa general Saṃjaya, the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals,
the divine son Maheśvara, Vajrapāṇi the lord of the Guhyakas, the great yakṣa general Māṇibhadra, Hārītī with her retinue of five hundred sons, the nāga king Anavatapta, and the nāga king Sāgara.

And many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of deities, with invisible bodies, went to where that king of men’s royal palace was adorned with various ornaments, and where that Dharma-preaching monk was— where the ground was strewn with flowers and purified,
and adorned with various ornaments— in every place where the Dharma-preaching monk [was].
This earth shall be strewn with flowers, purified, and adorned with various ornaments; wherever a Dharma-seat is prepared, there people will gather to listen to the Dharma.

"Venerable Blessed One, we four Great Kings, together with many hundreds of thousands of yakṣas and all these others, shall be united and will provide protection for that human king who has a virtuous friend as his companion, who is led toward what is wholesome, and who is a donor of the unsurpassed, great, and noble elixir— having been fully satisfied by this nectar-like flavor of the Dharma, and having satisfied him, we shall guard that human king."
We shall provide protection, acceptance, and guardianship; we shall perform rites for peace and well-being. We shall provide defense for that royal family, the city, and the realm;
we shall provide protection, acceptance, and guardianship; we shall perform rites for peace and well-being.
And we shall deliver that object from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions.
Venerable Blessed One, suppose there were some king of men,
and within the realm of that king of men this sovereign king of sūtras were to circulate;
and when, Venerable Blessed One, that king of men [listens to] this Sovereign King of Sūtras, the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama...
If one should not honor, revere, respect, or worship the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold [this teaching],

then they would not satisfy and pay homage to us— the four great kings— with these hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of yakṣas through this hearing of the Dharma and this nectar-like essence of the Dharma;
they would not cause these divine bodies of ours to increase in great splendor, nor would they generate for us vigor and strength.
"May they not increase our splendor, glory, and fortune within our bodies.

Furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, we four Great Kings, together with our forces and retinues and many hundreds of thousands of millions of yakṣas, will no longer provide protection for that realm.
Venerable Blessed One, if you neglect our realm, all the hosts of gods dwelling in that realm will likewise neglect it."
And the deities, venerable Blessed One, will abandon their respective domains.
In various regions, there will be manifold deprivations of resources;
there will be terrible upheavals caused by kings;
and all sentient beings throughout every land will become prone to strife.

People will become prone to quarreling, contentious, and fallen into dispute; various kinds of planetary afflictions and diseases will manifest in the realm. Meteors will appear, arriving from various directions, and the planets and constellations will become mutually adverse.
They will produce sun-like apparitions and lunar eclipses;
and the sun and moon, while constantly and perpetually situated within the expanse of the sky, will not be visible to sight.
Halos resembling the falling of meteors will appear in the midst of the sky from time to time;
there will be earthquakes,
and wells situated on the earth will dry up, their waters shrinking away.
Irregular winds will blow;
there will be irregular rains;
and famine and wilderness conditions will prevail throughout the entire realm.
And foreign armies will invade that realm;
it will become full of great distress.
O Venerable Blessed One, for us four Great Kings, together with our forces and retinues, and for many others—

When the hundreds of thousands of yakṣas and the gods and nāgas dwelling in that realm become indifferent toward that realm, then in that realm there will arise these various kinds of hundreds of calamities, or even thousands of calamities.
"O Venerable Blessed One, whatever human king there may be who wishes to provide great protection for himself," (Bagchi 49)
He would desire to experience various kinds of royal pleasures for a long time; being endowed with all happiness, he would desire to exercise sovereignty before long;
and he would desire to bring happiness to all the sentient beings dwelling within his realm.
He may wish to defeat all hostile armies;
he may wish to protect his realm with every form of happiness;
he may wish to exercise sovereignty according to the Dharma.
And he should desire to liberate his own domain from all fears, calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions.
Furthermore, O Venerable Blessed One, this king of kings of sūtras, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, should be heard by that human king.
Having heard it, he should honor, revere, respect, and worship those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold it.

And we, the four Great Kings, together with our armies and retinues, should be fully satisfied by this very accumulation of roots of merit from hearing the Dharma, and by this essence of the Dharma which has been made manifest.
And these divine bodies of ours must be made to increase by great splendor. For what reason?
Because, O Venerable Blessed One, that king of men must certainly hear this Suvarṇaprabhāsottama, the sovereign king of sūtras.

Venerable Blessed One, however many various treatises on mundane and supramundane matters have been presented by Brahmendra; however many various treatises have been presented by Śakra, the lord of the gods; and however many treatises on mundane and supramundane matters have been presented for the benefit of sentient beings by sages possessing the five superknowledges—[all these are surpassed by yours].
"Venerable Blessed One, compared to those hundreds of thousands of Brahmā-indras, many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śakras,
and all the hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sages possessing the five supernormal powers, the Tathāgata is more eminent and more distinguished;
he has extensively proclaimed this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the king of sūtras, for the benefit of sentient beings."
Just as he must exercise sovereignty over all the human kings residing in Jambudvīpa,
so that all sentient beings shall be established in happiness,
and so that all territories shall be free from oppression and devoid of thorns.
In such a way that the enemy armies will be defeated and turned back; and so that those territories shall be free from affliction.
And how all the phenomena within their realms will be free from affliction and free from calamity;
and how those kings of men will cause great torches of Dharma to blaze and be kindled within their own territories;
and how all the abodes of the devas—
They will be illuminated by the gods and the sons of gods;

and we four Great Kings, together with our armies and retinues, as well as many hundreds of thousands of yakṣas and the hosts of gods throughout all of Jambudvīpa, will be satisfied and gladdened; and great vigor, strength, and power will be generated within our bodies.
And just as they shall cause heat, splendor, and fortune to enter into our bodies in an even greater measure;
and just as all of Jambudvīpa shall become well-supplied with food, delightful, crowded with many people, and filled with inhabitants;
and just as all sentient beings dwelling in Jambudvīpa shall experience every happiness.
They will experience various delights;
and for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of incalculable eons, they will experience sublime and magnificent pleasures,
and they will come into the company of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

In the future time, they will fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment; all of that is now [manifested] by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, through the empowerment of the power of great compassion,

[including] hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Śakras, and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of hosts of sages possessing various and manifold kinds of all five superknowledges, who have surpassed the divine and reached the unsurpassed knowledge of a Tathāgata.

By that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is a Cātireka-samyaksaṃbuddha, through the empowerment of his exceedingly superior vows and ascetic penances, this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the foremost of sūtras, has been extensively proclaimed here in Jambudvīpa for the benefit of all sentient beings, accompanied by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Brahmās and Indras.
By that king of men, all worldly and supramundane royal affairs, royal treatises, and royal administrative acts pertaining to the entire Jambudvīpa were brought forth—
those by which these sentient beings will become happy.
All of those have been shown, elucidated, and fully revealed by the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened Buddha, in this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sūtras.
Therefore, O Venerable Blessed One, for that reason and by that cause, this king of men must certainly listen to this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the sovereign king of sūtras, with reverence;
he must honor it with reverence and worship it with reverence.
When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the four great kings:

"Therefore, O four great kings, together with your armies and retinues, you must certainly exert great effort for the sake of protecting those human kings who hear and honor this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras."

Great kings who uphold this sovereign of sutras— whether monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen— will manifest a Buddha-field nearby and perform the deeds of a Buddha for the world of gods, humans, and asuras.
They shall extensively proclaim this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras.
You four great kings must certainly provide protection for those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of sūtras;
you must provide their guardianship, defense, and support, as well as exemption from punishment, exemption from weapons, and peace and prosperity.
And so that the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of sutras may be protected, unoppressed, free from affliction and distress, and possessed of happy minds,
[may they] extensively proclaim this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras, to sentient beings.
Then indeed, the Great King Vaiśravaṇa, the Great King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the Great King Virūḍhaka,
and the Great King Virūpākṣa rose from their seats, draped their robes over one shoulder, arranged them as upper garments,
placed their right knees upon the ground, and with palms joined in reverence toward the Blessed One, at that moment faced him.
They praised the Blessed One with verses that were appropriate to the occasion.
To him whose body is as pure as the moon of the Jina, who possesses the radiance of a thousand rays from the sun of the Jina;
whose eyes are as stainless as the lotus of the Jina, and whose tips of teeth are as white and dustless as the kumuda lily and frost of the Jina.
The ocean of Jinas, which is like an ocean of the qualities of the Jinas, a mine of many jewels,
filled with the waters of the nectar of wisdom, and crowded with hundreds of thousands of samādhis.
Adorned with the wheel-marks on his feet like those of a Victor, and likewise possessing a thousandfold radiance;
his hands and feet are marked with webs, just as the king of swans has webbed feet.
We pay homage to the Victor, the Lord of Mountains, who shines like a mountain of gold, who is stainless as refined gold, and who is like Mount Meru in all his virtues. Suv_7.4.
Like the moon in the sky and like the moon reflected in water, we pay homage to the stainless Victor, the lunar Tathāgata, who is like an illusion and a mirage.
Then the Blessed One addressed the four great kings in verses:
This is the most excellent king of the lords of sūtras, the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama, [taught] by those possessed of the ten powers.
You, the world-protectors, must protect [them]. // Suv_7.6 //
So that this profound jewel of a sutra, which bestows happiness upon all sentient beings, may long circulate in this Jambudvīpa for the sake of the welfare and happiness of beings. (Suv 7.7)
And those beings in the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-system, having stilled the sufferings of the miserable states and the pains of the hells; Suv_7.8 //
And all the great kings who have gone here to Jambudvīpa, having given rise to great joy,
shall protect their realms with righteousness, so that this Jambudvīpa may become secure.
Abounding in food and delightful, all beings throughout Jambudvīpa shall be happy;
for that king who does not strive for his own dear pleasure within his realm, his sovereignty [shall endure].

One who desires sovereignty and popularity should listen to this king of sūtras, which brings about the destruction of the most formidable enemies; this sovereign of kings of sūtras dispels the supreme fear caused by hostile armies and removes calamities, bringing about the highest auspiciousness.
Just as a most beautiful jewel-tree, the source of all virtues, stands well-situated within a fine dwelling,
so too should this king of the best of sūtras be regarded as the source of royal qualities and the like. (Suv 7.12) (Bagchi 53)
Just as cool, pure water obtains the nature of removing heat,
so too does this sovereign of sūtras become a bestower of merit and happiness for kings.
Just as a casket of jewels containing all precious gems rests in the palm of one's hand,
even so is this sovereign king of sūtras, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, for the multitudes of kings.
This sovereign of sutras is honored by the hosts of gods and saluted by the lords of gods;
it is protected by the four world-protectors of great supernatural power.
This king of sutras is always held in mind by the Buddhas dwelling in the ten directions;
as one teaches this sutra, the Perfectly Enlightened Ones grant their approval.
Hundreds of thousands of yakṣas protect the realm in the ten directions;
with joyful and delighted minds, they listen to this sovereign of sutras.
The secluded hosts of gods residing in Jambudvīpa—
all those hosts of gods, let them hear this sūtra with joyful hearts.
By hearing that Dharma, they obtain the power of splendor and the power of vigor;
and with great majesty, they shall cause the divine bodies to flourish. (Suv 7.19)

Then, indeed, the four great kings, having heard these verses of such a nature from the presence of the Blessed One, were struck with wonder, filled with amazement, and moved with rapture; through the force of that Dharma, they wept for a mere moment, as it were, and shed tears.

With their bodies honored and their limbs and members in full bloom, and being endowed with inconceivable joy, happiness, and gladness, they once again scattered divine māndārava flowers over the Blessed One. Having scattered and strewn them, they rose from their seats, draped their robes over one shoulder, placed their right knees upon the ground, and, bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, [addressed him].
They said this to the Blessed One:

"Venerable Blessed One, we four Great Kings— each Great King with a retinue of five hundred yakṣas— will also always follow the Dharma-preaching monk, out of reverence for and protection of that Dharma-preacher."
Thus ends the seventh chapter, titled "The Chapter on the Four Great Kings," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Exalted Suvarṇaprabhāsa.
(Bagchi 55) // The Chapter on the Goddess Sarasvatī //

Then the Great Goddess Sarasvatī, having draped her robe over one shoulder and placed her right knee upon the ground, bowed with palms joined toward the Blessed One and addressed the Blessed One as follows:
"Venerable Blessed One, I too, the Great Goddess Sarasvatī, shall provide eloquence for that monk who is a preacher of the Dharma in order to adorn his speech,
and I shall bestow a dhāraṇī upon him."
I shall bring about the realization of the meaning of these well-expounded excellent words,
and I shall produce a great radiance of wisdom for the monk who is a Dharma-preacher;
whatever words or phrases may have fallen away from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the king of the best of sūtras.
And I shall restore all those [teachings] forgotten by that Dharma-preaching monk, with their well-expressed words, phrases, and syllables;
and I shall bestow upon him a dhāraṇī for the sake of preventing the loss of mindfulness,
so that this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the foremost of sūtras, may long circulate in Jambudvīpa for the benefit of those beings who have planted roots of merit under thousands of Buddhas.
And he shall not cause it to disappear quickly.
Furthermore, many sentient beings, having heard this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, and having reflected upon it, shall come to possess sharp wisdom;
they shall attain an inconceivable aggregate of knowledge, and their lifespan shall certainly not be short.
May they obtain prosperity;
may they receive immeasurable favor regarding their birth and an infinite mass of merit;
and may they become skilled in all treatises and knowledgeable in the methods of various arts and crafts.
I shall now describe this combined ritual for bathing for the sake of that Dharma-preaching monk and those beings who listen to the Dharma:
all afflictions caused by planets and constellations, birth and death, the turbidity of strife and quarrel during the Kali age, calamities, portents, nightmares, and the poison of water;
and all *kākhordas* and *vetālas* shall be pacified.
The wise ones bathe [the image] with medicinal herbs and mantras:
*vacā*, *gorocanā*, *spṛkā*, *śirīṣa*, *śyāmāka*, *śamī*, the highly auspicious *indrahastā*, *vyāghranakha*, *agaru*, and *tvac*. (Suv 8.1)
Nīveṣṭaka, sarjarasa, sihlaka, gulgulu resin, tagara, patra, śaileya, sandalwood, and red arsenic; Suv_8.2.
Samocaka, turuṣka, saffron, musta, mustard seeds,
narda, cavya, fine cardamom, uśīra, and nāgakeśara. (Suv 8.3)
One should grind these ingredients in equal proportions under the Puṣya asterism;
with these mantra-words, one should consecrate the powder a hundred times.
Namely: *Sukṛte karajātabhāge haṃsaraṇḍe indrajālamalilaka upasade avatāsike kutra kukalavimalamati śīlamati saṃdhibudhamati śiśiri satyasthite svāhā*.
Having prepared a mandala of cow dung, one should place loose flowers;
one should place [the image] in a golden vessel or a silver vessel with sweet [substances].
And one should station there four men clad in armor;
likewise, four well-adorned maidens should be stationed, each carrying a water-jar.
Constantly burning guggulu incense, one should employ the five kinds of musical instruments;
that goddess is thus fully adorned with umbrellas, banners, and flags.
One should employ arrows and spears until the boundary is reached;
then one should perform the binding of the boundary, and afterwards begin the ritual task.
One should undertake the binding of the boundary according to this sequence of mantra-words.
It may be as follows:
*ane nayane hili hili gili khile svāhā*.
Having bathed behind the Blessed One, one should perform the rite of bathing and pacification by reciting this mantra,
as follows: *sugate vigate vigatāvati svāhā*.
May those constellations that have set protect life in the four directions;
may the afflictions caused by birth under a constellation, or the fears arising from the karma of the zodiac signs,
and the terrible dangers born from the agitation of the elements, be pacified.
To the even and the uneven, svāhā!
To the Sugata, svāhā!
To the one born from the ocean, svāhā!
Svāhā to Skandhamāruta! Svāhā to Nīlakaṇṭha! Svāhā to Aparāhitavīrya!
Svāhā to the one born from the Himavat!
Svāhā to the one with unblinking wheels!

Homage to the Blessed One, the Brāhmaṇī; homage to the goddess Sarasvatī! May these mantra-words be effective; may they pay homage to that Brahman, svāhā! By means of this rite of bathing, for the sake of that Dharma-preacher, for those listeners of the Dharma, and for the sake of the scribes, I myself, together with the hosts of Gaganasiddhi yakṣas and gods, shall go there.
Whether in a village, a city, a town, or a monastery, I shall effect the pacification of all diseases everywhere.

I shall pacify all afflictions caused by planetary spirits, strife, impurities, and the influence of malevolent stars at birth; I shall pacify the afflictions of evil dreams and obstacles, as well as all *kākhordas* and *vetālas*.
Thus, there shall be the preservation of life for those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of sūtras.
May they attain both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa,
and may they become irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the Great Goddess Sarasvatī, saying, "Excellent, excellent, Sarasvatī, Great Goddess! You have set out for the welfare of many people and for the happiness of many people, in that you have spoken these [mantras] conjoined with medicinal herbs.
And the Great Goddess Sarasvatī, having paid homage at the feet of the Blessed One, sat down to one side.
Then, indeed, the great brahmin Kauṇḍinya, who had received the prophecy from his teacher, invoked that goddess Sarasvatī.
The great goddess Sarasvatī, of great asceticism, is worthy of worship;
she is renowned throughout all worlds, the bestower of boons, and possessed of great virtues.
Residing upon a mountain peak, the lovely woman, clad in a garment of darbha grass,
wears auspicious raiment and stands upon one foot.
May all the gods assemble and cause these words of the sutra to be spoken from their tongues for the sake of sentient beings, uttering auspicious speech.
It may be as follows: *Sure*, *vire*, *araje*, *arajavati*, *hi*, *gule*, *piṅgale*, *piṅgale*, *vatimukhe*, *marīcisumati*,
*diśamati*, *agrāmagrī*, *talavitale*, *ca*, *vaḍivicarī*, *mariṇipāṇaye*, *lokajyeṣṭhake*, *priyasiddhivrate*, *bhīmamukhiśacivarī*.
O Unobstructed One, O Unobstructed Intelligence! Namuci, Namuci, Great Goddess, accept this homage!
May the intelligence of all sentient beings be unobstructed; may my knowledge be perfected in the treatises, worldly sciences, the Piṭakas, poetry, and so forth.
It is as follows: *Tadyathā:* [The mantra follows]... Bagchi 58.
O you of great power, *hili hili mili mili*!

May she move about; may my *māyā* move about by the power of the Blessed Goddess Sarasvatī, for the sake of all sentient beings. O young maiden, *hili mili*, I invoke you, O Great Goddess, by the truth of the Buddha, by the truth of the Dharma, and by the truth of the Saṅgha.

By the truth of Indra, by the truth of Varuṇa, and by the truth of those who in this world are speakers of truth—with their word of truth, O Great Goddess, I invoke you! Hili hili mili! May my mantra-practitioners and the illusions of all sentient beings move about!
Homage to the Blessed Lady Sarasvatī! May the words of the mantra be effective; svāhā!
Then the great brahmin Kauṇḍinya, having received the prophecy from the Teacher, praised the Great Goddess Sarasvatī with these verses:
May all the hosts of spirits listen to me, for I shall praise the Goddess whose face is most excellent, supreme, and beautiful—
she who is the foremost and highest goddess among women in the world of gods,
gandharvas, and lords of asuras.
Named Sarasvatī, she has wide eyes and limbs adorned with various wonders;
radiant with merit and scattered with the qualities of wisdom, she is beautiful to behold with her many diverse and excellent features.
I shall praise her with distinguished qualities of speech— her who brings about accomplishment, who is most excellent and supreme,
who is truly praiseworthy, a mine of virtues, supremely pure, and radiant as a lotus.
To Sulocanā, whose eyes are supreme, who is the auspicious refuge, and who provides auspicious instruction;
to her who is adorned with inconceivable virtues,
who is like the moon, and whose radiance is stainless.
To her who is a mine of wisdom, to her who possesses the perfection of mindfulness, to the most excellent lion, to her who has a man as her vehicle;
to her whose arms are adorned with jewels and gems, and whose appearance is like the full moon. (Suv_8.17)
To her of pleasing speech and gentle voice, endowed with profound wisdom;
to her who possesses the supreme goodness that accomplishes the highest purpose; to her who is saluted and honored by gods and asuras;
to her who is worshipped by the abodes of all hosts of gods and asuras, and always fully adored by the multitudes of spirits.
Homage, svāhā!
O Goddess, I bow to you; may she bestow upon me a flood of virtues.
May all beings grant me distinguished accomplishment in all undertakings,
and may they always protect me and all sentient beings in the midst of enemies.
Rising at dawn with great vigor, one should recite these verses, which consist of complete syllables and full sentences;
thus, one shall obtain wealth and grain for all one's intentions and attain auspicious and sublime success. // Suv_8.20 //
Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Chapter on the Goddess Sarasvatī," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Exalted Suvarṇaprabhāsa;
[followed by] the Chapter on the Great Goddess.
Then the Great Goddess Śrī, having bowed down to the Blessed One, said this to him:
"Venerable Blessed One, I too, the Blessed Great Goddess Śrī, shall provide for the needs of that Dharma-preaching monk;

that is to say, with robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, as well as other articles, so that that Dharma-preacher shall be fully provided with all necessary supplies."
And he will attain freedom from impairment;
his mind will be healthy,
and he will pass his days and nights with a happy mind.
Furthermore, from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, he will bring forth and examine various kinds of words and syllables,
so that this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, may long endure in Jambudvīpa for the benefit of those beings who have planted roots of merit under thousands of Buddhas.
And it shall not quickly disappear;
there will be sentient beings who hear this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras,
and they shall experience for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of inconceivable eons divine and human happinesses.
Famine shall disappear and abundance shall appear;
and sentient beings shall be made happy with the provisions for human comfort.
May they come to encounter the Tathāgatas,
and may they realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment in the future;
may all the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama be utterly and completely severed.
There is a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Raktakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī,
in whose realm I, the Great Goddess Śrī, have planted roots of merit; by virtue of which,
he now dwells in whichever direction among sentient beings.
Whichever direction he looks upon with his gaze toward sentient beings,
and whichever direction he approaches,
in each and every such direction many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sentient beings shall become happy through every provision of comfort.
And they shall attain freedom from deficiency;
by means of food, drink, wealth, grain, gold, bullion, jewels, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, native gold, silver, and other such requisites,
all sentient beings will become fully endowed with every necessity through the power of the Great Goddess Śrī.
And one should perform worship for that Tathāgata;
perfumes, flowers, incense, and lamps should be offered.
The name of the goddess Śrī should be recited three times.
One should offer it incense, flowers, incense smoke, and lamps,
and various delicacies should be set before it;
thus, its great mass of wealth increases.
In this regard, the following is said:
The essence of the earth increases, and the earth is filled with joy;
the deities always become like a field abundant with fruits and grain.
The tree-deities cause the crops to grow in most wonderful ways.
The name of the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama, should be uttered;
the Great Goddess Śrī will take those beings under her care and will bestow great prosperity upon them.
In the capital city of Alakāvatī, in the Puṇyakusumaprabha garden grove, within the Saptaratnaprabhava palace named Suvarṇavarṇadhvaja, the Great Queen Śrī resided.
Any man who wishes to increase his heap of grain must thoroughly clean his own house.
One should be clothed in pure white garments and wear fragrant clothing.
One should recite the name of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī, three times.
Worship of him should be performed with the hand of the Great Goddess Śrī.
Flowers, incense, and perfumes should be offered,
and various kinds of food and dwellings should be provided.
And by the power of this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras, at that time the Great Goddess Śrī will attend upon his house.
And he will cause his great heap of grain to increase. Therefore, one who desires to invoke the Great Goddess Śrī should recollect these vidyā-mantras,
as follows:
Homage to all Buddhas of the past, future, and present! Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Homage to the Bodhisattvas beginning with Maitreya!
Having paid homage to them, I employ this spell: may this spell of mine be successful!
It is as follows:
O you who possess fulfilled boons, O you who go everywhere!
In the accomplishment of the great task, in the attainment of equality regarding the welfare of sentient beings,
there is the nature of arrival for the highly fortunate one;
it is like great splendor for the sake of benefit.
In that which is upheld by the ṛṣis; in the observance of the samaya.
These are the mantra-words of the nature of the head-anointing (mūrdhābhiṣeka-dharmatā).
There is one mantra-word of the moon-step, which is non-deceptive.

By those who possess concentration, who have planted roots of merit, and who maintain it while wearing [the robes], for seven years, during the morning, [the water] shall be endowed with eight qualities and five tastes.
In the afternoon,
having performed an offering of flowers, incense, and perfumes to all the Blessed Buddhas for the sake of fulfilling the knowledge of omniscience for oneself and for all sentient beings,
may all his intentions be fulfilled.
May they quickly prosper!
Having made that house clean, or having prepared a monastery or a forest retreat, one should make a mandala with cow dung and offer perfumes, flowers, and incense;
[one should provide] a clean seat.
It should be prepared;
flowers should be scattered there.
Then, at that very moment, the Great Goddess Śrī will enter and remain in that place.
Depending on that, in that house, village, city, town, monastery, or forest hermitage, they will never suffer any deficiency caused by anyone.
They will be made happy by all the requisites for well-being, through an abundance of gold, silver, jewels, wealth, grain, and all other necessities.
And their roots of virtue will be sustained.

Therefore, he must grant the entire mission sent by the great goddess Śrī through the power of her affection; she shall attend upon him there for as long as life lasts and will not delay, and she will fulfill all their intentions.
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "The Chapter on the Illustrious Great Goddess," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Exalted Suvarṇaprabhāsottama.
(Bagchi 63) // The Chapter on Retaining the Names of All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnaśikhin.
Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇaratnākaracchatraskūṭa. Homage to the Tathāgata Suvarṇapuṣpajvalaraśmikeṭu.
Homage to the Tathāgata Mahāpradīpa.
There is a bodhisattva named Ruciraketu;
there is a bodhisattva named Suvarṇaprabhāsottama.
The bodhisattva named Suvarṇagandha;
the bodhisattva named Sadāprarudita;
the bodhisattva named Dharmodgata.
To the east is the Tathāgata named Akṣobhya;
to the south is the Tathāgata named Ratnaketu;
to the west is the Tathāgata named Amitāyus.
In the north is the Tathāgata named Dundubhisvara.
Those bodhisattvas who uphold and recite these names of the bodhisattvas from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, shall always remember their past lives.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled "The Retention of the Names of All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Exalted *Suparṇaprabhāsottama*.
(Bagchi 64) // The Chapter on the Earth Deity Dṛḍhā //
Then the earth goddess Dṛḍhā said this to the Blessed One:

"Venerable Blessed One, wherever this Suvarṇaprabhāsottama, the king of the sovereign sūtras, shall now or in a future time enter— whether it be a village, a city, a town, a district, a forest region, a mountain cave, or a royal court— "
Wherever this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, shall be extensively proclaimed;
and wherever, Blessed One, on that patch of earth where a Dharma-preaching monk has set his body upright and prepared a Dharma-seat;
and wherever on that seat the Dharma-preacher, having sat down, shall extensively proclaim this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras.
In that regard, Blessed Lord, I, the earth goddess Dṛḍhā, shall come to those places on earth.
Seated here upon the Dharma-throne, with my body and head invisible, I shall place them beneath the soles of the feet of that monk who is a preacher of the Dharma.
And I shall satisfy myself by this hearing of the Dharma, by the nectar-like essence of the Dharma.
I shall honor and worship [them];

and having satisfied myself, honored myself, and gladdened myself by this hearing of the Dharma and by this nectar-like essence of the Dharma, [I shall extend it] from this mass of earth sixty-eight thousand yojanas in extent, up to the adamantine foundation of the earth.
"I shall cause it to increase by means of the essence of the earth; I shall honor it and bring it to fullness.
From above down to this surface of the earth bounded by the ocean, I shall moisten the entire circle of the earth with the unctuous essence of the earth.
And I shall make this great earth more vigorous."
By this, the various grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and forest trees in this Jambudvīpa will grow with greater vigor;
and all the various groves, trees, and crops will become more vigorous,
more fragrant, more succulent, more delicious, more beautiful to behold, and more magnificent.

And those beings, having consumed those various kinds of food and drink, will increase their lifespan, strength, complexion, and faculties. Being endowed with splendor, strength, complexion, and beauty, they will perform, rise up for, and carry out many hundreds of thousands of various earthly tasks;
they will perform deeds that require great effort.
For that reason, O Venerable Blessed One, all of Jambudvīpa will become secure;
it will be well-supplied with food, prosperous, flourishing, delightful, crowded with many people, and filled with inhabitants.
Furthermore, all sentient beings throughout Jambudvīpa will be happy.
They will experience various and manifold delights;
those beings will also be endowed with splendor, strength, complexion, and beauty.

For the sake of this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras, they shall approach those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen who uphold this king of sutras while they are seated upon their Dharma-thrones.

Having approached with hearts full of faith, for the sake, benefit, and happiness of all sentient beings, they shall entreat those Dharma-preachers to proclaim this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras;
then I, the earth goddess Dṛḍhā, together with my retinue, shall become more powerful and majestic.
Therefore, O Venerable Blessed One, great strength, vigor, and power will be generated within our bodies;
and brilliance, glory, and fortune will enter our bodies.
And when I, the earth goddess Dṛḍhā, am thoroughly satiated by this nectar-like essence of the Dharma, O Venerable Blessed One, [the world will be refreshed].
Having attained great splendor, power, heroism, strength, and momentum, this great earth will cause this Jambudvīpa, seven thousand yojanas in extent, to flourish with a great essence of the earth;
and the great earth shall become more vigorous.
And, O Venerable Blessed One, all these beings, depending upon the earth, shall attain growth, development, and expansion; they shall become great.
And having become great, all these beings dwelling upon the earth shall enjoy various kinds of resources and enjoyments, and shall experience happiness.

And may they enjoy all these various and manifold comforts of requisites— consisting of diverse foods, drinks, edibles, garments, beds, seats, clothing, houses, celestial palaces, gardens, rivers, lotus ponds, springs, lakes, pools, and so forth— which are of such a nature, established upon the earth, manifested on the earth, and resting upon the earth.
Therefore, O Venerable Blessed One, for that reason all sentient beings should practice gratitude toward us.
This *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, must certainly be heard with reverence, honored, revered, esteemed, and worshipped.
And when, O Venerable Blessed One, all those sentient beings go forth from various clans and various households, they shall approach those Dharma-preachers.
Having approached, they shall hear this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras.
And having heard it, those beings, having returned to their respective various families, houses, villages, cities, and market towns, shall say to one another once they have reached their own homes:
"Today we have heard a profound teaching of the Dharma."
"Today we have acquired an inconceivable mass of merit;
by hearing this Dharma, we shall be liberated from the hells,
and today we have been completely freed from the animal realm, the world of Yama, and the domain of hungry ghosts."

By means of this hearing of the Dharma, they will, in the future, throughout many hundreds of thousands of births, be sustained by rebirths among gods and humans. And having been born in various households, [they shall,] from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sūtras, for the sake of those sentient beings— even down to...
They might proclaim even a single illustration, or at least a single chapter, or a single previous account, or at least a verse of four lines,
or at least a single word from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras; they might cause other beings to hear it, or at the very least,
they might cause other beings to hear even the name of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras.
"Venerable Blessed One, wherever those various kinds of beings, in various regions of the earth, might announce to one another these various causes of sūtras,
cause them to be heard, and engage in conversation regarding them,"
"Venerable Blessed One, all those regions of earth will become more vital and more supple.
In all those various regions of earth, manifold essences of the earth and all kinds of requisites for all sentient beings will arise in great abundance, increase, and reach full maturity."
All those beings will become very wealthy and possess great enjoyments; they will be devoted to giving and will have deep faith in the Three Jewels.

When this had been said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the Earth Deity, Dṛḍhā: "O Earth Deity, whatever beings from here might hear even a single word from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sūtras, they, having passed away from this human world, will be reborn among the various classes of the gods in the Heaven of the Thirty-three."
They shall be reborn among the hosts of gods.

O Earth Goddess, whatever beings would adorn those places for the sake of this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras— the places adorned even with a single parasol or a single piece of fine cloth— those divine abodes shall be so adorned.
In those seven classes of gods belonging to the desire realm, divine palaces made of the seven precious gems and adorned with every ornament will be established;
those beings, having passed away from this human world, will be reborn in those divine palaces made of the seven precious gems.
And in each of those divine palaces made of the seven precious gems, they will be reborn as seven excellent earth-deities and will experience inconceivable divine pleasures.
When this had been said, the Earth Deity Dṛḍhā addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"Therefore, O Venerable Blessed One, I, the Earth Deity Dṛḍhā, shall dwell upon those patches of earth where that Dharma-preaching monk, seated upon his Dharma-seat, resides, remaining invisible in my physical form."
I shall place my two soles upon the head of that Dharma-preaching monk,
so that this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, may long circulate in Jambudvīpa for the benefit of those beings who have planted roots of merit under thousands of Buddhas,
and that it may not quickly disappear.
And if sentient beings should hear this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras,
they shall experience inconceivable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of divine and human pleasures throughout many future eons,
and they shall come to dwell in the presence of the Tathāgatas.
May they awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment in the future,
and may all the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama be utterly and completely eradicated.
Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled "The Chapter on the Earth Deity Dṛḍhā," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Glorious Suvarṇaprabhāsottama.
(Bagchi 68) // The Chapter on the Great Yakṣa General Saṃjñeya //

Then, indeed, the great yakṣa general named Saṃjñeya, together with twenty-eight great yakṣa generals, rose from his seat, draped his robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee upon the ground, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, addressed the Blessed One as follows:

"Venerable Blessed One, this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, shall circulate now and in the future in whatever village, city, town, district, or region of a district, or forest retreat, mountain cave, royal court, or house it may be."
In that regard, Blessed Lord, I, the great yakṣa general named Saṃjñeya, together with twenty-eight great yakṣa generals,
will approach that village, city, town, district, forest, mountain cave, or royal court. With my body made invisible, I shall provide protection for that monk who is a preacher of the Dharma.
I shall provide protection, guardianship, and preservation; I shall effect the avoidance of punishment and the avoidance of weapons, and I shall perform rites for peace and well-being.
And for all those listeners of the Dharma—men, women, boys, and girls—who have heard from this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of sutras, even a single four-line verse, at the very least...

If even a single word from the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the foremost of sūtras, should be heard or memorized— even the name of a single bodhisattva, or the name of a single Tathāgata, or at the very least, the name of this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the foremost of sūtras— should be heard or memorized, I shall provide protection for all of them.
I shall provide protection, acceptance, preservation, exemption from punishment, exemption from weapons, and peace and well-being.

And for those families, those houses, those cities, those villages, those market towns, those forests, and those royal households, I shall provide guarding, protection, acceptance, preservation, exemption from punishment, exemption from weapons, and peace and well-being.
By what cause is it that all phenomena have been fully understood and all phenomena have been realized,
as many as all phenomena may be?
And how all phenomena exist,
and what all phenomena are,
and how all phenomena are correctly known.
"Venerable Blessed One, I have direct perception regarding all phenomena.
Venerable Blessed One, the illuminations of my wisdom are inconceivable;
the light of my wisdom is inconceivable."
The movement of knowledge is inconceivable;
the aggregate of knowledge is inconceivable.
Venerable Blessed One, my sphere of knowledge regarding all phenomena proceeds in an inconceivable manner.
And just as all phenomena have been rightly known by me, O Venerable Blessed One,
rightly examined, rightly fully understood,
rightly scrutinized, and rightly awakened to;
For that reason, O Venerable Blessed One, the name Saṃjñeya arose for me, the great yakṣa general Saṃjñeya.
"Venerable Blessed One, I shall provide eloquence for the sake of adorning the speech of the Dharma-preacher monk;
I shall infuse vital energy into the pores of his skin,
and I shall generate great stamina, strength, and vigor within his body."
I shall produce an inconceivable radiance of knowledge for him;
I shall awaken his mindfulness;
and I shall grant him great enthusiasm.
And so that this Dharma-preacher may not have a weary body,
but may have a body with joyful faculties and be filled with great rapture.

By this means, may this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, circulate for a long time in Jambudvīpa for the benefit of those beings who have planted roots of merit under thousands of Buddhas,
so that it does not quickly disappear;
and may beings hear this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras.
May they attain the inconceivable aggregate of knowledge;
may they become possessed of wisdom;
and may they grasp an immeasurable aggregate of merit.
In the future, for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of inconceivable eons, they shall experience divine and human pleasures;
they shall come into the presence of the Tathāgatas in the future and fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment;
and all the sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama shall be utterly and completely severed.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled "The Chapter on the Great Yakṣa General Saṃjñeya," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Exalted Suvarṇaprabhāsottama.
(Bagchi 70) // The Chapter on the Treatise of the King of the Samaya of the Lord of Gods //
Homage to that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Ratnakusumaguṇasāgaravaiḍūryakanakagirisuvarṇakāñcanaprabhāsaśrī.

Homage to that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, whose body is adorned with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of manifold virtues, and for whom this torch of Dharma blazes. Homage to that Great Goddess Śrī, who is endowed with immeasurable merit, grain, and auspiciousness.
Homage to that goddess Sarasvatī, who is endowed with immeasurable qualities and wisdom.
Then, at that time and on that occasion, King Baladaketu said this to his son Ruciraketu, who had recently been consecrated and established in the kingdom:
"My son, there is a treatise on royal policy called *Devendrasamaya*,
which I previously acquired from my father, King Balendraketu, when I had recently been consecrated and established in the kingdom."

By means of that royal science known as the *Devendrasamaya*, I exercised sovereignty for twenty thousand years. I do not recall, even for a duration of a single moment of thought, anyone previously established in unrighteousness.
What, then, is this royal science called the *Devendrasamaya*?
Then, O Kuladevatā, at that time and on that occasion, King Baladaketu extensively proclaimed to his son, King Ruciraketu, this treatise on statecraft called *Devendrasamaya* through these verses.
I shall proclaim the treatise on royal polity, which brings about the welfare of all sentient beings,
cuts through all doubts, and destroys all evil deeds.
Having become joyful in heart here, all you kings individually,
with palms joined in reverence, listen to the samaya of all the lords of gods.
On this king of mountains, Vajraprākāra, at the assembly of the lords of gods,
Brahmendra was questioned by the world-protectors who had arisen.
You are our teacher of the gods, you are Brahmā, you are the lord of the deities;
you are the dispeller of doubts, so please sever our doubt.
(71) How is it that a king born among humans is called a god? For you, O King, are born here in this world of men. (Suv_13.5)
"How will he exercise sovereignty among gods and humans?"—
thus was Brahmendra questioned by the World-Protectors.
Brahmā, the preceptor of the gods, spoke here to the world-protectors:
"Since I have now been questioned by the world-protectors here regarding the welfare of all sentient beings, I shall proclaim this supreme treatise."
I shall explain, having applied my mind, the origin of men in the abode of humanity,
and by what cause kings arise within their realms.
By the empowerment of the lords of gods, he shall enter his mother’s womb;
having first been empowered by the gods, he subsequently enters the womb.
Furthermore, although a king is born and passes away in the world of humans,
he is indeed said to be a son of the gods, having originated from the gods.
Indeed, a portion was granted to the king by the Trāyastriṃśa gods and the lords of the deities;
you, O lord of men, were created as a son together with the gods.
For the sake of pacifying unrighteousness, he is the preventer of evil deeds;
he shall establish sentient beings in virtuous conduct for the purpose of sending them to the abode of the gods.
Whether a human, a god, a gandharva,
a lord of men, a rākṣasa, or even a caṇḍāla, he is the one who restrains evil deeds.
You are like a mother or a father to those who perform good deeds, O King;
you perceive the ripening of their fruits, being sustained by the lords of the gods.
You perceive the ripening fruits of good and evil deeds in this very life, and you are sustained by the kings of the gods.
For when a king overlooks wrongdoing committed within his realm,
he should not fail to inflict various forms of punishment upon that sinful people;
for by neglecting those who act wickedly, unrighteousness increases greatly.
Deceit and quarrels will further arise in the kingdom,
and the lords of the gods will become enraged in their abodes in the Heaven of the Thirty-three. (Suv 13.17)
For when a king overlooks wrongdoing that has become firmly established in his realm,
the realm is destroyed by terrible, deceitful, and most cruel [evils].
And that kingdom perishes when attacked by a foreign army,
along with its enjoyments, its forces, and whatever wealth has been accumulated.
They employ various forms of deceit and rob one another;
for the sake of that very purpose for which he holds kingship, he will not perform his duty,
but destroys his own kingdom like a lordly elephant destroying a lotus pond.
Irregular winds blow, and irregular rains fall;
the planets and constellations, as well as the moon and the sun, likewise become irregular. (Suv 13.21)
Grain, flowers, fruits, and seeds do not ripen properly;
famine occurs there where the king is indeed indifferent, and the gods become displeased in their celestial abodes. (Suv 13.22)

For when a king overlooks evil conduct as it spreads abroad, all those kings of the gods will speak to one another: Suv_13.23. When a king overlooks evil conduct as it spreads abroad, all those kings of the gods will speak to one another.
For this king is unrighteous and has taken his stand on the side of non-dharma;
before long, this king will surely provoke the wrath of the deities.
Due to the intense provocation of the deities, his realm will perish;
moreover, weapons and unrighteousness will prevail within this realm.
Deceit, quarrels, and diseases arise;
the Lord of the Gods becomes incensed, and the deities will neglect him.
When a kingdom is devastated, that king falls into grief;
he suffers the loss of loved ones, whether through a brother or a son.
One will experience separation from a beloved wife, or perhaps the birth of a daughter;
likewise, meteors will fall and suns will appear as reflected images. (Suv 13.28)
Or there may be fear of enemy armies, and famine increases greatly;
beloved ministers die, while those who are disliked roar out their words.

The sons will seize the beloved objects of their father, the consoling words of their mother, and the family wealth and possessions from one another, while being at odds with their young wives. (Suv 13.30)
In every land they shall slay one another with weapons;
disputes, quarrels, and deceits shall arise among the people of the realms.
A planet enters the kingdom, and a terrible disease arises;
immediately thereafter, those worthy of initiation will become unrighteous.
His ministers and members of his assembly will likewise be unrighteous;
in that interval, honor will be paid to unrighteous people.
The suppression of righteous beings will certainly occur;
there will be honor for unrighteous people and the suppression of those who follow the Dharma.
Therein, three things become provoked: the stars, the waters, and the winds.
Three things perish when unrighteous people hold power:
the essence of the true Dharma, the vitality of sentient beings, and the vital sap of the earth.
Honor for the untruthful and contempt for the truthful—
these three things will prevail there; furthermore, famine will be intense, and during that interval, the flavor and vitality of fruits and crops will not exist.
In that realm, sentient beings will for the most part be afflicted by illness;
even the sweet and large fruits there will become scarce, bitter, and indeed pungent.
Formerly delightful things— play, laughter,
and pleasures— as well as beautiful assembly halls, will become agitated by hundreds of hardships.
The oily quality and flavor of grains and fruits will diminish; thus, the elements of the body and the sense faculties will no longer be so nourished. (Suv 13.39)
Sentient beings will be ill-favored in complexion, possessing very little strength and being extremely weak;
even after eating a great deal of food, they will find no satisfaction.
In that interval, beings do not obtain strength, power, or vigor;
they become deficient in energy regarding sense objects.
Sentient beings will become afflicted by disease, oppressed by various ailments;
there will be planetary and stellar influences arising from various rākṣasas.
The king would become unrighteous, established on the side of non-dharma;
he would be at odds with the three realms throughout the entire mandala of the triple world.
And many such faults as these would arise within his realm.
When a king who stands upon his side of righteousness neglects wrongdoing—
that very purpose for which a king is indeed presided over by the lords of the gods— is not fulfilled; for one who neglects wrongdoing, there is no true kingship.
Through good deeds they are reborn in the abodes of all the gods and asuras;
through evil deeds they go among the hungry ghosts, animals, and in the hells.
In the realm of the Trāyastriṃśa gods, they suffer torment because of their evil deeds.
For when a king overlooks the evil committed by those dwelling in his realm,
he becomes guilty toward the ancestors and the kings of the gods; neither the state of being a son nor the exercise of kingship has been fulfilled.
Even when a task is ruined by most cruel deceits,
the king remains established there, O Lord of Gods, as the abode of humanity.
The king is one who pacifies misdeeds and promotes good deeds;
he is the producer of karmic results for sentient beings in this very life.
For he who demonstrates the various kinds of ripened fruits of well-performed and ill-performed actions is indeed called the King, the agent.
It was presided over by the hosts of gods and rejoiced in by the lords of the gods.
For his own sake, for the sake of others, for the sake of the Dharma, and for the sake of the realm,
as well as for the sake of subduing the deceitful and wicked people within the kingdoms.
One should renounce even life, kingdom, and sensory objects for the sake of Dharma;
and one should not, out of ignorance, neglect a person who knows what is unrighteous when questioned about it.
And there is no other destruction in this world so terrible as that which arises from deceit— the suppression of the wilderness of guile.
Furthermore, most cruel deceits will arise in this realm,
and that kingdom will be plundered like a great lake by elephants.
The lords of the gods become enraged and the abode of the gods is plundered;
indeed, all conditions within the realm become adverse.
Therefore, the punishment of evildoers should be proportionate to their offense;
one should protect the kingdom with righteousness and never practice unrighteousness.
Even at the cost of his own life, let him not fall into sin;
toward his kinsmen, strangers, and all the people of the realm,
let the king be impartial, and let him not fall into partiality.
The righteous king shall fill the three worlds with his fame,
and the lords of the gods will rejoice in the realms of the Thirty-three.
Likewise, in Jambudvīpa, our son is a righteous king;
he governs the realm with dharma and establishes the people in virtuous conduct.
And by his good deeds, the king sends that person here;
he fills the abode of the gods with gods and sons of gods. (Suv 13.59)
Our king, greatly gladdened, governs the kingdom according to the Dharma;
the lords of the gods become pleased and protect those rulers of men.
The constellations move correctly, as do the moon and the sun;
the winds blow at the proper time, and in this way, it rains at the proper time.
They bring abundance to the kingdom as well as to the abode of the gods;
the celestial realm becomes filled with immortals and the sons of immortals.
Therefore, a ruler of men should renounce even his own dear life so that he may cause the jewel of Dharma to turn again, by which the world shall become happy.
He who is adorned with virtues should practice righteous service;
being ever free from evil, he serves [the king] who is always pleased.
He should protect the kingdom with righteousness and instruct it in righteousness;
he should establish beings in well-done deeds and restrain them from ill-done deeds.
"The kingdom becomes well-supplied with food, and the king becomes majestic;
he exercises restraint upon evildoers in a manner that is appropriate.
The king becomes renowned and protects his subjects in happiness. (Suv 13.66)
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled "The Royal Treatise on the Convention of the Lord of Devas," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Exalted Suvarṇaprabhāsa.
(Bagchi 77) // The Chapter on Susaṃbhava //
When I became a universal monarch, O King, I then renounced the earth together with its oceans;
those four continents, filled with jewels, were offered by me to the former Victors.
And there was no dear or pleasing thing that I had not previously sacrificed for the sake of seeking that Dharma-body throughout many eons, even my own beloved life.
Just as in inconceivable past eons, during the teaching of the Sugata Ratnaśikhin,
after that Sugata had passed into parinirvāṇa, there was a king named Susaṃbhava.
That universal monarch, the lord of the four continents who rules over the earth bounded by the oceans,
that elephant among kings, was then asleep in the royal capital at the sound of the Conqueror’s voice.
Having heard the qualities of the Buddhas within a dream, one beholds the Dharma-preacher Ratnoccaya,
standing in the midst of the sun, resplendent and illuminating this king of sutras.
Having awakened from his dream, the king’s entire body was suffused with joy;
he departed from the royal palace and approached the supreme assembly of disciples.
He makes offerings to the disciples of the Jina and inquires about the Dharma-preacher Ratnoccaya:
"Where in this noble Saṅgha of monks is the one named Ratnoccaya, who is endowed with such virtues? (Suv 14.7)
In that interval, Ratanoccaya was indeed seated elsewhere within another cave;
comfortably settled, he was reciting this king of sutras, which contains various jewels.
In that interval, they pointed out to the king the Dharma-preacher, the monk Ratnoccaya,
who was seated elsewhere within a cave,
blazing with the splendor of those rays.
O Ratnoccaya, this Dharma-preacher here maintains the profound domain of the Victor;
he shall constantly proclaim the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama-sūtra-ratna*, the king of all sūtras.
Having bowed at the feet of Ratanoccaya, King Susaṃbhava spoke thus:
"O Pūrṇaśaśāṅkacakra, please teach me the supreme jewel of a sūtra, the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama."
Ratnoccaya accepted the request of that very King Susaṃbhava;
and all the deities throughout the entire trichiliocosm became filled with great joy.
On a supreme and distinguished portion of the earth, sprinkled with water scented with perfumes and containing jewels,
that lord of men, having strewn the ground with flowers, then took his seat there.
Then that throne of the king was beautifully adorned with parasols, banners, and many thousands of bells;
they strewed that throne of the king with various wonderful and excellent flowers and moon-blossoms. (Suv 14.14)
The gods, nāgas, asuras, and kiṃnaras, as well as yakṣas, lords of yakṣas, and mahoragas,
then showered that seat with divine rains of māndārava flowers.
Inconceivable and infinite thousands of millions who had come from the highest celestial realms out of desire [for the teaching],
having gone forth, strewed *sāla* flowers over the Exalted Ratnoccaya.
And that Dharma-preacher Ratnoccaya, his limbs radiant with beauty and clothed in pure garments,
approached that seat and, with palms joined, paid homage.
The gods, lords of gods, and deities rained down māndārava flowers;
hundreds of thousands of inconceivable musical instruments resounded while remaining in the sky.
Having ascended and sat down, that Dharma-preacher, the monk Ratnoccaya,
called to mind the inconceivable thousands of millions of Buddhas in the ten directions.
He should constantly generate compassion for all sentient beings and cultivate a mind of mercy; and during that time, he should proclaim this sutra to King Susambhava as well. Suv_14.20.
Standing with palms joined in reverence, the king who had rejoiced [in the teaching] through body, speech, and mind,
his eyes overflowing with tears born of the impulse of the True Dharma, his body became radiant.
And for the sake of honoring this sutra, Susaṃbhava, the king,
having taken a wish-fulfilling jewel-king at that time, made a vow for the sake of all purposes.
May there be rain here today in Jambudvīpa, along with the seven jewels and ornaments;
and may the beings who are here in Jambudvīpa indeed become happy and very wealthy.
Within that interval, the seven precious jewels were rained down upon the four continents,
as well as armlets, necklaces, excellent earrings, and likewise food, drink, and garments.
And having seen that rain of excellent jewels falling upon Jambudvīpa,
King Susaṃbhava offered the four continents, filled with jewels, into the teaching of Ratnaśikhin.
And I was that Tathāgata Śākyamuni who was once a king named Susaṃbhava;
it was by him that the earth, including the four continents filled with jewels, was then renounced for my sake. (Suv 14.26)
He was the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, and that Dharma-preacher was the monk Ratnoccaya;
it was by him that this sūtra was revealed during the time of King Susaṃbhava.
This sutra which I have heard was, within that interval, approved with one-pointed speech;
by that very wholesome karma of mine, through that hearing and approval of what was heard. (Suv 14.28)
May I obtain a body of golden hue, endowed with the marks of a hundred merits, always pleasing to behold,
delightful to the eyes, lovely for people to see, and a source of joy for thousands of millions of gods.
For ninety-one billion eons, I was a universal monarch;
for many thousands of millions of eons, I experienced sovereignty over the three worlds.
For inconceivable eons I was Śakra, and likewise Brahmā and Indra with a tranquil mind; I have pleased immeasurable Buddhas, the number of whom can never be known.
(82) Thus, the great mass of merit that I have heard and rejoiced in through this sutra is such that,
according to my intention, I have attained awakening and have indeed realized the body of the true Dharma. (Suv_14.32)
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled "The Excellent Origin," in the Sovereign King of Sutras, the Glorious Suvarṇaprabhāsottama.
(Bagchi 83) // The Chapter on Protection through the Refuge of Yakṣas //

O Śrī Mahādevī, whoever— whether a faithful son of good family or a daughter of good family— should desire to perform an inconceivable, great, vast, and extensive worship with all necessary requisites for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present;
or who should desire to fully comprehend the profound sphere of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, of the past, future, and present.
Therefore, in that region, whether in a monastery or in a forest retreat, wherever this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, is being proclaimed in detail,
one should listen to this *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*, the king of the sovereign sūtras, with an undistracted mind and with ears not turned away.
Then the Blessed One, wishing to illuminate this very matter more extensively, at that time spoke these verses:
Whoever wishes to perform an inconceivable worship of all the Buddhas, and to bring forth an understanding of the profound sphere of activity of all the Buddhas— Suv_15.1 //
Having traveled to all regions, they shall enter monasteries and dwellings wherever this supreme *Suvarṇabhāsa* Sūtra is being taught.
This sutra is inconceivable, an ocean of infinite virtues;
it is the liberator of all sentient beings from the ocean of manifold sufferings.
I see the beginning of this sutra, as well as its middle and its end;
this sovereign of sutras is exceedingly profound, and no simile for it exists.
Neither by the dust of the Ganges, nor on the earth, nor in the ocean,
nor for one situated in the expanse of the sky can any comparison whatsoever be made.
Immediately thereafter, one should enter by means of the entrance into the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu),
wherein there is a stūpa consisting of the Dharma, profound and well-established.
And there, in the midst of this stūpa, one shall see the Jina Śākyamuni proclaiming this sūtra with a pleasing voice. (Suv 15.7)
For as many as are the incalculable and inconceivable millions of eons,
one indeed experiences the very pleasures of gods and humans.
When he should know thus: "Whatever is heard there in the sutra, in this way an inconceivable mass of merit has been accumulated by me. (Suv 15.9)
One who would endure intense pain to hear this sutra even once might as well stride across a full hundred yojanas filled with pits of fire.
As soon as one has entered the monastery or likewise a dwelling,
all evils and the signs of all bad dreams depart.
The affliction of planets and constellations, as well as the terrible *kākhorda* and planetary portents—
all these turn away immediately upon his entrance.
One should prepare such a seat there, resembling a lotus,
just as it was shown by the Naga kings within the dream.
There, having sat upon a seat, one should proclaim this sutra;
one should read it as written, and likewise master it.
Having descended from his very seat, he would go to another place;
yet the miraculous displays were seen even there, remaining upon that seat.
And sometimes the form of a Dharma-preacher is seen there;
sometimes the form of a Buddha, and sometimes that of a Bodhisattva.
On that seat, forms of Samantabhadra appear in some places, likewise those of Mañjuśrī, and in others, forms of Maitreya are seen.
In some places there is only a mere appearance, and in others the manifestation of a deity;
they are seen for a moment and then vanish again.
The teaching of the Buddha is everywhere conducive to complete accomplishment and is highly praised;
it is endowed with fortune and auspiciousness, and brings victory in battle. (Suv 15.19)
He shall fill this entire Jambudvīpa with his glory,
and all his enemies shall be utterly defeated in every way.
His enemies are always defeated, he is forever free from all evil,
he is ever victorious in battle, and he rejoices in glory.
Brahmā, Indra, and the lords of the thirty-three gods, as well as the guardians of the world;
Vajrapāṇi, the lord of the yakṣas, and Saṃjñeya, that bull among men.
The Naga king Anavatapta and likewise Sāgara;
the lords of the Kinnaras, the lords of the gods, and likewise the lords of the Garuḍas—
taking these as their leaders, all the deities as well.
And they shall always worship that inconceivable Dharma-stūpa;
seeing it, those beings will be filled with joy and reverence.
All those supreme lords of the gods will likewise think thus, and all those deities as well will say to one another: Suv_15.25 //
Behold all these people, who are gathered here through the accumulation of splendor, glory, and merit;
they have come here by virtue of having planted roots of goodness.
Those who have come here for the sake of hearing this profound sūtra,
possessing inconceivable faith and reverence for the Dharma-stūpa.
These are the compassionate ones in the world; these are the benefactors of sentient beings;
they are the food of the essence of the true Dharma for those of profound teachings.
Through the entry into the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu), those who enter it, those who hear this sūtra, and those who cause others to hear it [attain this]. (Suv 15.29)
Hundreds of thousands of Buddhas were previously worshipped by them;
through this root of merit, they hear this sūtra. (Suv 15.30)
All those lords of the kings of gods, as well as Sarasvatī, Śrī, Vaiśravaṇa, and likewise the four great rulers; Suv_15.31 //
Hundreds of thousands of yakṣas, possessing supernatural powers and great strength,
will protect them day and night without weariness.
And by the Yakṣa lords of great power, Nārāyaṇa and Maheśvara,
and twenty-eight others headed by Saṃjñeya.
Hundreds of thousands of yakṣas, endowed with supernatural powers and great strength,
will provide protection for them in all situations of fear and danger.
And Vajrapāṇi, the lord of yakṣas, together with five hundred yakṣas and all the bodhisattvas, will provide protection for them.
And Maṇibhadra, the lord of yakṣas, as well as Pūrṇabhadra;
Kumbhīra and Aṭāvaka, and the very powerful Piṅgala.
And each lord of the yakṣas, surrounded by five hundred yakṣas,
will provide protection for those by whom this sūtra has been heard.
The Gandharva Citrasena, Jinarāja, Jinarṣabha, Maṇikaṇṭha, Nīlakaṇṭha, and Varṣādhipati as well; Suv_15.38.
Mahāgrāsa, Mahākāla, and likewise Svarṇakeśin;
Pāñcika, Chagalapāda, and likewise Mahābhāga.
Praṇālī, Mahāpāla, Markaṭa, and Vāli,
as well as Sūciroma, Sūryamitra, and likewise Ratnakeśa.
Mahāpraṇālī, Nakula, Kāmaśreṣṭha, and Candana;
Nāgāyana, Haimavata, and likewise Sātāgiri.
(87) All of them possess supernatural powers and great strength and prowess;
they will provide protection for those who hold this sūtra dear. Suv_15.42.
For Anavatapta, the lord of nāgas, and likewise Sāgara; Mucilinda and Elāpattra, both Nanda and Upananda; Suv_15.43.
Hundreds of thousands of nāgas, possessing supernatural powers and great strength,
will provide protection for them from every danger and terror.
Valī, Rāhu, Namuci, Vemacitra, Saṃvara, Prahrāda, Kharaskandha, and other lords of the asuras.
Hundreds of thousands of powerful and miraculous asuras will provide protection for them against the terrors and fears of calamities.
Hārītī, the mother of spirits, together with her five hundred sons and those established as the seven mothers, will provide protection for them.
Caṇḍā, Caṇḍālikā, Yakṣiṇī, and likewise Caṇḍikā;
Dantī, Kūṭadantī, and she who robs all beings of their vital energy.
All these possess miraculous powers and great strength and prowess;
they will provide protection for them on all sides in the four directions.
Sarasvatī and the foremost deities, as well as the inconceivable ones,
likewise Śrī and all the other deities.
The Earth itself is a deity, as is the presiding deity of fruits and grain;
so too are the deities dwelling in groves, trees, shrines, and rivers. (Suv 15.51)
All those hosts of deities, with minds full of great joy,
will provide protection for those who hold this sūtra dear.
And those beings are endowed with longevity, complexion, and strength; they constantly adorn themselves with glory, merit, majesty, and fortune.
They pacify all afflictions caused by the planets and constellations,
and they destroy all misfortune, evil, and bad dreams.
The Earth Deity herself, profound and of great strength,
was satiated by the flavor of this sovereign king of sutras, the *Suvarṇaprabhāsottama*. (Bagchi 88) *Suv_15.55*
The essence of the earth increases by sixty-eight thousand and hundreds of yojanas,
reaching as far as the place of the vajra-base.
And for a full hundred yojanas in front, the earth becomes moistened from above by the power of hearing this sutra. (Suv 15.57)
And all the deities, stationed throughout the ten directions,
were satiated by the flavor of this supreme king of sūtras, the Suvarṇaprabhāsottama.
They become endowed with vital energy, excellent, and possessed of fortune, vigor, and strength;
they are gladdened by happiness and provided with various flavors.
Throughout this entire Jambudvīpa, the deities of the fruits, the crops,
and the forests will be filled with great joy upon the proclamation of this sutra.
Grains, grasses, and various flowers,
as well as diverse fruit-bearing trees, grow forth on every side.
All fruit-bearing trees, groves,
and forests shall be made to blossom beautifully, gladdened by various fragrances.
With diverse flowers and diverse fruits as well,
all the grasses and forest trees cause growth upon the surface of the earth.
Throughout this entire Jambudvīpa, inconceivable numbers of naga maidens,
arisen with joyful hearts, approached the lotus ponds.
They cause various lotuses to grow in all the lotus ponds— namely,
